body.statement:
For every even integer \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\).  There exist symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) and such that \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\).  Moreover, there are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c/K\leq E_K\leq C/K\).

source.verbatim_statement: For any given even integer k>0, there exist two probability measures ν_0 and ν_1 on [-1,1]: ∫t^l ν_1(dt)=∫t^l ν_0(dt), l=0,...,k; ∫|t|ν_1(dt)-∫|t|ν_0(dt)=2δ_k; δ_k=β_* k^{-1}(1+o(1)).

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-04 from the primary arXiv v1 TeX/HTML source 1105.3039, Lemma 1 and the immediately following Bernstein-constant statement; δ_k is defined there as best uniform degree-k approximation error for |x|.
